# Chapter XXIII: *Of the Deep above the Earth.*

And as the qualifying <term>The "qualifying" or "fountain" spirits are Boehme's terms for the fundamental forces or attributes of God that interact to create reality.</term> or fountain spirits of God always took their power and strength out of or from the Body of Nature, so the Angels also always took their power and strength out of or from the Nature of God.

96. And as the Holy Spirit in Nature forms and fashions <note>original: "Imageth or frameth"</note> everything, so the spirit of the Angels also united <note>original: "qualified"</note> with the Holy Spirit and helped to form, fashion, and shape everything, so that all might be of one heart and will, and a pure delight and joy. For the Angels are the children of the great God, whom He has generated in His Body of Nature to multiply the divine joy.

97. But here you must know that the bodies of Angels cannot grasp the birth or generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note> of God, nor does their body *understand* it; only their spirit understands it. But the body remains still, just as the *Nature* in God does, and lets the spirit work together and labor with God, and play lovingly.

98. For the Angels play before and in God, as little children play before their *parents*, by which the divine joy is increased.

99. But when that mighty, powerful prince and king, *Lucifer*, was created, he would not do so; instead, he elevated and puffed himself up, wanting to be God alone. He kindled the wrath-fire <term>In Boehme's cosmology, the "wrath-fire" represents the harsh, dark, and consuming aspect of the divine nature when separated from love and light.</term> within himself, and so did all *his angels also.*

<margin>right hand</margin>
100. But when that was done, he roared with his kindled fire-spirit throughout the Nature of God, and then the whole Body in the Nature of God—as far as his kingdom and dominion reached—was kindled. But because his light was instantly extinguished, he could no longer unite <note>original: "qualifie"</note> with his spirit in the two births or generations <note>original: "Genitures"</note>, *namely* <note>original: "viz."</note>, of the Son

103. ## *Of the Kindled Nature.*

106. But God has therefore kindled Nature so much and so intensely, and kindled the burning of His wrath within it, so that He might thereby build a dwelling for the devils and keep them *prisoners* there. Since they were children of wrath, He must rule over them with His fierce zeal or jealousy, and they also exist within the wrath of God.

# The Twenty-Fourth Chapter.

<margin>Printed Copy: Concerning the dead nature and the fourth day.</margin>
## *Of the Incorporation or Condensing <note>original: "Compaction"</note> of the Stars.*

-> 1. <-

**N**ow when the whole body of Nature in the vast space or circumference of this world was numbed or deadened as if in a hard death—even though Life was *hidden* within it—God moved the whole body of the nature of this world on the fourth day. He generated the stars from or out of Nature, through the risen light. For the wheel of God’s birth <note>original: "geniture"</note> moved itself again, just as it had done from eternity.

<summary>This page describes God’s creation of a "dwelling house" for devils within the "kindled" or wrathful aspect of nature and explains how the stars were formed on the fourth day of creation as the "wheel" of God's generative power began to move again.</summary>

# Of the Incorporation of the Stars. Chapter 24.

### 2.
Indeed, it had moved on the *first day* and began the *birth* or *generation* <note>original: "geniture"</note> within the *body* of corrupt nature. For on the *first day*, life separated itself from *death*; on the *second day*, a firmament was *created* between them; and on the *third day*, *life* broke forth through *death*. For there, the light broke forth through the *darkness* and caused the dead body of *nature* to spring, flourish, and become active and agile.

### 3.
For on the *third day*, the *body of nature* labored <note>original: "travell"</note> so hard in anxiety until the *love-fire* kindled itself within *death*, and until the *light of life* broke forth through the *congealed body of death* and sprang up out of *death*. But on the *third day*, it stood only in the *fire-crack* <term>fire-crack: a sudden, explosive flash of energy or light that marks the transition from darkness to life</term>, from which mobility originated.

### 4.
On the *fourth day*, the *light* rose up and made its seat in the *house of death*, and yet *death* could not—and cannot—comprehend it. Just as the austere *birth of God*—which stands in the innermost kernel from which life exists—cannot grasp the meekness and the light of that meekness along with the *Spirit* in the meekness, so also the dead *darkness* of this world cannot comprehend the *light of nature*; nor can the *devils* either.

<margin>*or, divine body.</margin>
### 5.
But the light shines through *death* and has made its *royal* seat in the midst or center of the *house of death* and of *God's wrath*. It generates for itself a *new divine body* <note>original: "Body of God"</note> out of the house of wrath; this body exists eternally in the *love of God*, remaining incomprehensible to the old, kindled *body* in the outermost *birth* or *generation* <note>original: "geniture"</note>.

# Chapter XXIV: On the Incorporation of the Stars

->Now you will **ask**:<-
->“How shall I understand this?”<-

->*Answer*<-

6. I cannot write it in your heart at all, for it is not within every person's capacity, understanding, or apprehension—especially where the spirit stands in the "House of Wrath" and does not interact <note>original: "qualifie"</note>, operate, or unite with the Light of God. But I will show it to you through an earthly comparison <note>original: "similitude"</note>, so that you might, if possible, grasp a little of the *deep meaning* <note>original: "sense"</note>.

7. Look at and consider a tree: on the outside, it has a hard, thick <note>original: "grosse"</note> rind or bark that is dead and numb, lacking growth <note>original: "vegetation"</note>. Yet it is not entirely dead, but in a state of weakness or frailty <note>original: "imbeccillity"</note>; there is a great difference between it and the trunk <note>original: "body"</note> which grows just beneath the rind or bark. But the trunk has its **living power** and breaks through the withered rind, generating many beautiful young shoots <note>original: "bodys"</note> or twigs, all of which remain within the old trunk.

8. But the *rind* is, as it were, dead; it cannot comprehend the life of the tree but only hangs upon it, acting as a cover for the tree where worms take shelter <note>original: "harbour"</note>, which eventually destroy the tree.

9. The whole "house" of this world is just like this: the outward darkness is the House of God’s Wrath, where the devils dwell, and it is truly the House of Death, for the Holy Light of God has died within it.

### Of the Incorporation of the Stars. Chap. XXIV.

10. But the Body of this great House, which lies hidden under the *shell* or *rind* of darkness—in a way that is incomprehensible to darkness—*that* is the House of Life, where Love and Wrath wrestle with one another.

11. Now, Love always breaks *through* the House of Death and generates *holy, heavenly twigs* in the Great Tree. These twigs stand in the Light, for they spring up through the shell or *skin* of darkness, just as twigs grow through the shell or bark of a tree, and they are *one life with God*.

12. And Wrath also springs up in the House of Darkness, and it holds many a noble twig *captive* in Death through its infection in the house of *fierceness* <note>original: "fiercenesse"</note>.

13. And this is now the *sum* <note>original: "Summe"</note> or the content of the Astral Birth or Geniture <note>term: "Geniture" refers to the process of generation, birthing, or the natural formation of things</note>, about which I intend to write here.

->*And now it may be asked:*<-

->What are the stars? Or from what have they<-
->come to be?<-

14. They are the *power* of the seven Spirits of God. For when the wrath of God was kindled by the Devil in this world, then the whole *house* of this world in Nature—or the outermost birth or geniture—was, as it were, numbed or *chilled* in Death; it is from this that the *earth* and *stones* originated. But when this hard dross or *scum* was driven together into a lump or heap, then the *Deep* was cleared, but it was very dark, for the light within it was dead in the wrath.

15. But now the Body of God, regarding this world, could not *remain* in Death, but God moved himself

*But you must understand this profound matter correctly!*

16. The *Light* of God, which is the *Son* of God, as well as the Holy Spirit, *did not die*. Instead, the Light—which went forth from the heart of God *from eternity* and enlightened Nature (which is generated from the seven spirits)—departed from that harsh, corrupted Nature. Because of this, the nature of this world, with its tangibility and physical form, has *remained* in death. It cannot grasp the Light of God but is instead a dark house of devils.

17. Therefore, on the fourth day of Creation, God *regenerated* the entire house of this world and its qualities. He placed the fountain spirits within this house of darkness so that he might once again generate a *new body* out of it for his own praise, honor, and glory.

18. For his purpose was to create another angelic host out of this house. This was to be achieved in the following way: he would create an angel named *Adam*, who would generate creatures *like himself*. These creatures would inhabit the "House of the New Birth." In the middle of time, their King <note>Referring to Christ.</note> would be born from a human body to rule this newborn kingdom as a sovereign over these creatures, replacing the corrupted and expelled Lucifer.

24. For within and upon the Earth, all things were to spring up and generate themselves anew—as we see in mineral ores, stones, trees, herbs, and grass, and all kinds of animals—fashioned according to a heavenly image or form.

25. And although those images were temporary <note>original: "transitory"</note>, because they were not pure before God, yet at the end of this time, God would extract and draw forth the heart and the core <note>original: "kernel"</note> out of the new birth or generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note>. He would separate it from death and wrath, and this new birth would eternally spring up in God—outside and distinct from this place—and bear heavenly fruits once again.

26. But the death within the Earth and the wrath inside it were to be Lord Lucifer’s eternal house after the completion of this new birth or generation. In the meantime, Lord Lucifer was to lie captive in the darkness of the deep above the Earth; that is where he is now, and he may very shortly expect his inheritance <note>original: "Portion"</note>.

27. And so that this new birth or generation might be accomplished, whether the Devil wants it or not, the Creator has therefore generated himself within the body of this world—as if in the form of a creature—through his qualifying or fountain spirits <note>In the author's theology, these are the seven primary divine forces that drive all creation.</note>. All the stars are nothing other than God’s powers, and the entire body of this world consists of the seven qualifying or fountain spirits.

# Chap. XXIV. Of the Incorporating of the Stars.

42. For until the *third* day from the time that God's wrath was ignited in this world, Nature—in its state of distress—was a *dark valley* and remained in Death. But on the third day, life broke through Death, and the *New Birth* began.

43. For that long—and not an hour longer—***the newborn King and Grand Prince of this world,*** **JESUS CHRIST,** ***rested in Death.*** He has birthed, or generated, the first *three* days of the Creation of Nature and that specific time, bringing it out of Death and back into Light. He did this so that this time might once again be *one* Time with Eternal Time, ensuring no "Day of Death" stands *between* them. He also intended for the Eternal Love and the newborn (or regenerated) Love emerging from the new Body of Nature to be *one* Eternal Love. There should be no difference between the eternal Love and the newborn Love; instead, the newborn Love reaches into the Being or Substance that existed from eternity, existing within eternity itself.

44. Thus, the newborn Love—which rose out of the water of Life in the light *within* the stars and *within* the whole body of this world—is entirely bound and united with the eternal, beginningless, infinite Love. Together, they are *one* Heart and *one* Spirit, which supports and preserves everything.

45. # Chapter 25: *Of the whole Body of this Astral World.*

->*Now observe.*<-

14. The entire house of this world, which exists in a visible and comprehensible or *tangible* <note>original: "palpable"</note> state, is the old *House of God*, or the Old Body. This body existed before the time of wrath in a *heavenly clarity* <note>original: "claritie," meaning divine brightness or glory</note> and *brightness*. But when the Devil stirred up the wrath within it, it then became a house of darkness and of death.

# Of the Whole Body of This Astral World. Chapter XXV.

46. Dear Reader, I understand the *astrologers'* meanings and sayings full well, and I have also perused their writings and taken notice of how they describe the course of the *Sun* and *stars*. I do not despise this, but hold it to be good and right for the most part.

47. But if I write differently than they do in some matters, I do not do it out of stubbornness, conceit, or guesswork—doubting whether it is so or *not*. I dare not have any doubt in this, nor can any man instruct me in it.

48. I have *not* gained my knowledge through *study*. Indeed, I have read about the order and position of the *seven planets* in the books of astrologers and find them to be *very* accurate. But as for their root—how they came to be and from what they proceeded—I cannot learn that from any man, for they do not know it themselves. Neither was I present when God created them.

49. But because the doors of the deep, the gates of wrath, and the chambers of death are set open *in my spirit* through the love of God, the spirit must therefore look through them.

50. Accordingly, I find that the birth or *geniture* <note>original: "Geniture"; the process of generation, birth, or the natural order of creation</note> of nature remains the same to this day. It generates itself just as it first began. Every life, whether good or bad, takes its origin this way.

51. For this is the *right* or law of the Deity: that every life in the body of God should generate itself in *one* manner or uniform way. Though this is done through many *various* imaginings <note>original: "Imagings"; likely referring to the diverse forms or "ideas" through which life is expressed</note>, yet the *life*

# Chap. XXV. Of the Sun and the other Planets.

<margin>* The Sun <note>original: *sol*</note></margin>
[Ju]piter, as also Mars, by reason of their great orbital circumference and great height, cannot do it, because they stand so high above and far distant from the **SUN**.

-> *How it may be asked,* <-
-> what is the SUN, and what are the other <-
-> PLANETS? or how did they <-

67. Behold! the other *Planets* are distinct bodies <note>original: "peculiar Bodys"</note> of their own which have a physical property <note>original: "corporeal proprietie"</note> of themselves, and are not bound to any settled or fixed place, but only to the circle, orb, or sphere wherein they run their course. -> *Understand it correctly.* <-

68. The place where the SUN is, is such a place as you may choose or imagine anywhere above the Earth; and if God should ignite the Light by the Heat, then the whole world would be just such a Sun. For that same power in which the *Sun* stands *is everywhere, all over;* and before the time of wrath <note>In this context, "wrath" refers to a theological concept where the harsh, fiery qualities of nature became dominant over the gentle divine light.</note>, it was everywhere, all over in the place of *this world*, as bright as the *Sun* is now, but not so unbearable <note>original: "intolerable"</note>.

79. Now, the *astrologers* write that the planet *Mars* stands about 15,750 miles away from the *Sun*. I do *not* contradict this because I do *not* concern myself with the measuring of orbits <note>original: "Circles"</note>. Then *it* too was captured by the Light, stayed there, and took possession of that place.

80. The reason the Light could *not* take hold of it any sooner was because of its intense fierceness and sudden flash; it was not captured by the *Light* until the Light had completely and thoroughly influenced and possessed it.

81. And there it remains now, like a raging tyrant and stirrer of the whole body of *this* world. For that is its very duty <note>original: "Office"</note>: that with its *revolution* in the wheel of Nature, it moves and stirs everything, and from this, all life takes its origin.

*But you must understand this thing correctly:*

83. It was the power of the Light that remained in this place, which is a very gentle, friendly, gracious, lovely, blessed, and sweet Being. 84. The power of *Life* reached out this far from the *Sun*, and *no* higher; but its luster or *shining*—which also has its own power—reaches even to the *stars* and through the entire body of this world.

### Chapter XXVI. Of the Planet Venus.

*But you must here understand this high thing.*

21. The birth, rising, or springing up of the seven planets and of all the stars is no different than how the life and wonderful proportion, variety, and harmony of the Deity has generated itself from eternity.

22. For when King Lucifer caused this place of the world to be designated as a house of wrath for himself, and intended to rule there fiercely and powerfully, the Light in Nature immediately went out. He had expected to be the lord there, but instead, all of Nature was numbed <note>original: "benumm'd"</note> and frozen like a body of death in which there was no movement; he was forced to remain there in darkness as an eternal captive prisoner.

23. However, the Holy God would not allow this part of his body—meaning **the space or room of this world**—to remain in eternal darkness and shame <note>original: "ignominie"</note>, nor would he leave it to the devils as their own property. Instead, he generated a *new* government <note>original: "Regiment"</note> or dominion of Light, and of all the seven qualifying or fountain spirits <note>In the author’s cosmology, these are the seven primary forces or "Source-Spirits" that constitute the divine nature and the created world.</note> of the Deity. The devil could neither understand, seize, nor touch this new order, nor was it of any use or profit to him at all.

24. For he can no longer see in the light of the *sun*, but only in the darkness, because he did not become a creature in this light; therefore, it is not profitable or useful to him.

25. Since there had to be a new government or dominion, it necessarily had to be one that the devil could not grasp or touch, and one that he could not use as his own physical property.

# Chapter XXVI: Of Man and the Stars

113. Just as a man casts a *glance* on a woman, and a woman on a man, so the spirit of the man—meaning the *root* of love, which, in the rising up of life out of the *water*, rises through the *fire*—meets the woman's spirit. Thus, one spirit catches the other in that *oil* of the heart. From this, a *mass*, *seed*, or a driving will and desire to *propagate* a human being once again immediately arises within that *mass* <note>original: "Masse"; here referring to the embryonic substance or fertilized seed</note>.

114. The first *mass* <note>the original substance of the first human, Adam</note> also came to be in exactly such a way and manner. The Love-Spirit in the Heart of God cast a *glance* into the body of the kindled, wrathful Father <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "wrathful Father" represents the harsh, fire-like first principle of divine nature</note> upon the *water* of life. Through this, and out of this, *love* arose and sprouted in the *fire-flash* <note>original: "fire-Flash"; the moment of spiritual ignition or the spark of life</note> *before the time of the wrath*.

115. In this casting of the *glance*, the one spirit caught the other. The unctuous *oil* or water within the wrath *conceived* from the Love-Spirit in the Heart of God and qualified, mixed, or united with it. Then, the astringent <note>original: "astringent"; the contracting or "binding" force of nature</note> spirit drew the *mass* together. At that point, there was clearly a birth—a will or desire to produce a whole creature—just as the *seed* is within a man.

116. But now, the firmament of heaven that is *between* the Heart of God and the kindled, hard "chamber of death" was closed or shut up. If it were not, the life within the *mass* would have suddenly ignited itself.

117. For the firmament was *within* the *mass* as well as *outside* and *distinct* from the *mass*. This firmament is the parting mark or limit of *separation* between the Heart of God and the fierce devils <note>the forces of chaos, darkness, or destruction</note>.

118. Therefore, the Word or Heart of God had to breathe into the moving spirit in the *mass*, which was not done until the *sixth day*, for very certain and assured causes.

119. 120. But there was a fear that what happened to that once-fair son *Lucifer* would happen again—that the physical fountain spirits in the *Mass* would be ignited in the *wrath-fire* <note>the consuming, harsh aspect of divine energy or judgment</note>.

123. 135. This extract had *not yet* become Earth, though it was the *Salitter* of the Earth; rather, it was held or sustained by the *Word*.

136. For when the Love-Spirit from the heart of God glanced upon the *Salitter* of the *Mass*, then the *Salitter* caught hold of it and conceived from it, and was impregnated in the center of the soul. The *Word* stood in the *Mass* as a sound, but the *Light* remained in the center of the *Mass*, in the firmament of heaven, staying hidden in the unctuous oil <note>an archaic term for a rich, life-giving spiritual essence</note> of the heart. It did *not* move itself out of the firmament of heaven during the birth of the qualifying or fountain spirits.

137. Otherwise, if the *Light* had ignited itself in the birth or creation <note>original: "Geniture"</note> of the soul, then all seven qualifying or fountain spirits—according to the eternal birthright of the Deity—would have triumphed and interacted, mixed, or *united* in and with the Light, and would have been a *living angel*. But because "the wrath" <note>referring to the dark, harsh principle or divine anger that had entered the material world</note> had clearly already infected the *Salitter*, there was a danger of the same fate that befell *Lucifer*.

<summary>This page describes the pre-physical existence of the human soul as a divine seed within the "Mass" of heaven, explaining its composition from the Word of God and the "Salitter." It highlights the delicate balance of divine light within this substance, which was kept hidden to prevent the soul from falling into the same prideful wrath as Lucifer.</summary>

# Chap. XXVI. Of Man and the Stars.

Understand that it is not in the power or capacity of any person to discern or to know it, if the **Dawning** or *Morning-Redness* <note>original: "Morning-Rednesse." This refers to the *Aurora*, a central concept for Boehme representing the beginning of divine enlightenment within the human spirit.</note> did not break forth in the center of the soul.

143. For these are *divine mysteries* which no person can investigate by their *own* reason. I also consider myself most unworthy of such a gift; furthermore, I know I shall face many scorners and mockers, for *corrupted nature is horribly ashamed* in the presence of the Light.

144. But for all that, I cannot hold back. For when the divine Light breaks forth in the circle or birth of life, then the qualifying or fountain spirits <note>original: "qualifying or fountain Spirits." These are the fundamental source-energies or "Quellgeister" that Boehme believes drive both the cosmos and the human soul.</note> *rejoice*. In the circle of life, they reflect or look back into their Mother, into *Eternity*, and they also look forward into eternity.

145. But it is not a constant and lasting thing or being—a permanent clarifying or brightening of the qualifying or fountain spirits, much *less* of the *animal body* <note>original: "Bestial Body." This refers to the physical, mortal body and its base instincts.</note>. Rather, it is the *ray of God's light breaking through with a fiery impulse*, which rises up through the gentle water of life in love and remains standing in its heaven.

146. Therefore, I can bring it no further than from the *heart* into the *brain*, before the princely throne of the senses. There it is *shut up* within the firmament of heaven and does *not* go back again through the qualifying or fountain spirits into the mother of the heart, so that it might reach the tongue. For if that were possible, I would speak it with my mouth and make it known to the world.

*The Dawning or Morning-Redness* <note>original: "Morning-Rednesse"; this refers to Böhme's first book, "Aurora"</note> *arises from infancy and childhood, and shows or demonstrates the creation of all beings—but very mystically and not with sufficient clarity. ->Note<-

*This book is written with a magical sense or understanding for the author himself alone, who knew of no other readers. He supposed he produced this work only for himself, but God has disposed of it otherwise.*

->Note.<-

The *author* expressed the first syllable *MER* in the word *MERCURIUS* with an *A*, as *MAR* (*MARCURIUS*). This was not without a special mystical cause related to the first vowel *A*. But because those who are "wise in reason" <note>meaning those who rely on intellectual logic rather than spiritual intuition</note> and self-conceited dislike it—viewing it as merely a vulgar country expression—the transcriber of the High German <note>original: "High Dutch", which in the 17th century referred to the German language</note> copy from which this was translated wrote it according to the commonly accepted word, *MERCURIUS*.

### The Gate of the Deity.

->*Observe here the hidden Mystery of God.*<-

48. When you behold the Deep above the Earth, you should not say that it is not the Gate of God, where God dwells in His *holiness*. No, no, do not think so! For the entire holy Trinity—God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—dwells in the center under the Firmament of Heaven, yet that very Firmament cannot contain Him.

49. Indeed, everything is as if it were *one* Body: the outermost and innermost birth, along with the firmament of heaven, as well as the *astral birth within it* <note>Boehme uses "astral birth" to refer to the influence of the stars and the psychic or intellectual realm</note>. In and with this astral birth, the wrath of God also operates <note>original: "qualifieth"</note>, mixes, and unites; yet, they relate to one another like the governance, frame, or constitution within *Man*.

<margin>* Note: Three types of births or "genitures" in humanity.</margin>

50. 1. The *flesh* signifies the outward birth or "geniture" <term>geniture: a term Boehme uses for the process of coming into being or a specific state of existence</term>, which is the house of death. 2. The second birth or geniture in humanity is the *astral*, in which *life* exists and where *love* and wrath wrestle with one another. Up to this point, a person can know themselves, for the astral birth generates life in the outermost part—that is, in the dead flesh. 3. The third birth is generated between the astral and the outermost, and that is called the animated or *soulish* birth or geniture, or the *Soul*.

<summary>Jacob Boehme explains that God's presence permeates the physical world even though the "Firmament" cannot contain Him. He further draws a parallel between the cosmos and human nature, identifying three distinct levels of being: the fleshly, the astral, and the soulish.</summary>

90. The word **Wasser** <note>German for "water." The author uses the phonetic components of the word to explain spiritual and physical realities.</note> is thrust forth from the heart and closes the teeth together. It passes *over* the astringent <note>The "astringent" (harsh) and "bitter" qualities are two of the seven fundamental properties of nature in the author's theological system.</note> and bitter qualities and touches them *not*, but goes forth *through* the teeth. But when the spirit is *almost* entirely gone forth, then the astringent and bitter spirit contracts and rouses itself, and only then qualifies with the word. 91. But now, since the spirit conceives itself at the heart, comes forth, and closes the teeth together, and *hisses* with the tongue through the teeth, it signifies that the *Heart of God* has moved itself and made a *closure* <note>a boundary or encircling limit</note> around it, which is the *Firmament of Heaven*. Also, just as the teeth shut and close together and the spirit then goes through the teeth, so also the spirit goes forth from the heart into the *Astral Birth* <term>Astral Birth</term> <note>The "astral birth" or "geniture" refers to the generation of the stars and the cosmic order from the divine essence.</note>.

92. And as the tongue frames itself for the hissing, and qualifies, mixes, or unites with the spirit and moves with it, so the soul of man *co-images* <note>original: "co-Imageth"; to form a mental or spiritual image in union with another power</note> or frames itself with the Holy Spirit. It qualifies, operates, or unites with it, and presses jointly together in its power through *Heaven*, and also rules together with it in the *Word* of God.

# Chapter 21
## Concerning the Third Day

->I.<-

1. Although **the Spirit** in the writings of **Moses** has kept the **deepest mysteries** secretly hidden and concealed within the **literal letter**, yet everything is described so precisely that there is **no defect** at all in its **order**.

2. For when God, through the Word, had created Heaven and Earth and had separated the Light from the Darkness—giving a place to each of them—then **each** immediately began its own **birth** <note>original: "Geniture"; the process of coming into being or generation</note>, functioning, or operating.

3. On the **First Day**, God drove together [or compacted] the corrupt <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter is a term used by the author to describe the divine "soil" or essential substance of the spiritual world, which became corrupted into physical matter.</note> which resulted from the flaring of His wrath. I say, God then drove it together or created it through the **strong spirit**; for the word <term>Schuff</term> <note>original: "Schuff"; the German word *Schuf*, meaning "created." The author interprets the etymology as a "driving together."</note> signifies here a "driving together" [or compaction].

4. In this driving together or compaction of the corrupted wrath-Salitter, King **Lucifer** was also driven—as a powerless prince together with his angels—into the "hole" of the wrath-Salitter. # The Twenty-Third Chapter.
## Of the Deep above the Earth.

->I.<-

<margin>p. 70, 71, 110 p. 1193</margin>
**W**hen man looks at the *Deep* <note>The "Deep" refers to the vast expanse of the sky or the celestial cosmos.</note> above the Earth, he sees nothing but *Stars* and *Clouds* of *water*, and then he thinks, "Surely there must be another place where the *Deity* presents or shows forth itself, together with the *heavenly* and *Angelic Government*." He insists that the *Deep*, together with its *regiment* <term>rule or governance</term> or *Dominion*, be separated from the *Deity*; for there he sees nothing but *Stars*, and the *regiment* or *Dominion* between them is *Fire*, *Air*, and *Water*.

2. Then he immediately thinks, "God has made this in this way from his *predetermined purpose*, out of *Nothing*; how then can *God* be in this *existence*? Or, can that be *God Himself*?" He continually imagines that this is only a *House* where *God* rules and dwells by his *Spirit*: *God* cannot be such a *God* whose being consists of the power of this *government* or *Dominion*.

3. Many will dare to say, "What *kind* of *God* would that be, whose *Body*, *Being*, and *Power* or *virtue* <note>original: "vertue," referring to the inherent essence or effective power of a substance.</note> consists of *Fire*, *Air*, *Water*, and *Earth*?"

# Chapter XXIII. Of the Deep above the Earth.

They are all seven, every one of them—the first, second, third, fourth, and last. Yet, I must list them one after another in a way a creature <note>original: "creaturely way," referring to a human or finite perspective</note> can understand; otherwise, you could not grasp it. For the Deity is like a wheel with seven wheels, one inside the other, where a person sees neither beginning nor end.

->Now Observe:<-

## I.

19. First, there is the *astringent* quality <note>original: "astringent," meaning a contracting or drawing-together force</note>. It is *always* generated from the other six spirits. In itself, it is hard, cold, and sharp like salt—yet far sharper. A created being cannot fully grasp its sharpness because it never exists *singly* or alone in a creature. However, based on the nature of the ignited hellish quality, I know *how it is*. This astringent, sharp quality attracts or draws things together. Within divine love, it holds or retains forms and images, and dries them so that they remain stable or fixed.

## II.

20. The second generation is the *sweet water*, which is also generated out of all six spirits. It is the gentleness <note>original: "Meeknesse"</note> produced by the other six. It presses itself into the astringent birth <note>original: "Geniture," or the process of generation</note> and *always* ignites the astringent quality again, then quenches and softens it. This prevents it from becoming too astringent, as it would be in its own sharpness if the water were not there.

## III.

# Of the Deep above the Earth. Chapter XXIII.

# The Gate of the Holy Trinity.

## 67. The whole Birth or <term>Geniture</term>
<note>original: "Geniture"; this term refers to the eternal process of "begetting" or "generation" within the Godhead, through which all things are brought into being.</note> which is the Heaven of all Heavens, as also this world (which is *in* the Body of the whole), as also the place of the Earth and of all creatures, and whatever you can think of—***all that together is God the Father.*** He has neither beginning nor end. Wherever and whatever you think upon, even in the smallest circle that can be imagined, there is the whole Birth or Geniture of God, occurring perfectly, incessantly, and irresistibly.

68. But if the light is extinguished in a creature or in any place, then the <term>austere</term> <note>original: "austere"; in this context, it refers to the harsh, rigorous, or "dark" quality of nature that exists when it is not illuminated by divine light.</note> Birth or Geniture is *there*, which lies hidden in the Light in the innermost kernel. ***And this now is One Part.***

## 69. The second part or the second Person is the Light,
which is continually generated from or out of all powers. It enlightens all the powers of the Father again and possesses the fountain of all powers. But it is distinguished from the Father as a *distinct Person*, in that it cannot encompass the entire Birth or Geniture of the Father, and yet it is the Father's *Son*, who is always generated from or out of the Father. You have an instance of this in all the **lit fires** in this world; simply consider them.

## What moved Lucifer to this, so that he would want to be above God?

->*Answer.*<-

96. Here you must know that from *outside* <note>original: "without"</note> himself, he had no impulse at all toward his pride, but his beauty and brightness *deceived him*. When he saw that he was the fairest and most beautiful prince in heaven, he then *despised* the friendly, harmonious <note>original: "qualifying"</note> mixing, operating, and generating of the Deity, and thought to himself that he would rule with his princely power over the whole Deity, and that everyone must stoop and bow to *him*.

97. But when he found that he could not accomplish this, he then ignited himself, intending to do it *in some other way*. ## Of the Second Son,

<margin>* Avarice</margin>
# * Covetousness.

98. The second will was <term>covetousness</term><note>original: "Covetoufneffe"</note>, which grew out of pride; for Lucifer thought to himself that he would reign over all kingdoms as the only God. ### Of the Fourth Son
## *Wrath.*

<margin>* or Anger.</margin>
102. This son is the very *burning* hellish fire, and takes its origin also from pride. 103. Much could be written about this, but you will find it more clearly explained <note>original: "apprehensibly"</note> in the section concerning the Creation. For there, enough *living* testimonies are to be found so that no one need doubt whether these things are so or not.

104. Thus King *Lucifer* is the beginning of *sin*, the *sting* of *death*, the kindling of God’s wrath, and the beginning of all evil—a corruption, perdition, and destruction of this world. Whatever evil is done, *he* is the primary author and *cause* of it.

### Of the Miserable State of Corrupt Nature. Chapter 17

8. The moving or boiling spirit, which previously functioned or operated very meekly in nature, became very elevating and terrible in its outermost generation. In this outermost birth, it is now called the **Wind**, or the element of **Air**, because of its elevation and expansion.

16. In the same way, the **earth** and **stones** have their descent. For when the **Salitter** kindled itself in Nature, then everything became very rugged, thick, and dark, like a thick dark mist or cloud, which the astringent quality dried into hardness with its coldness.

17. From this, **Death** entered into Nature, so that Nature—or the corrupt earth—could no longer help itself. Thereupon, another creation...

## Ch. XVII. Of the miserable state of Corrupt Nature.

20. Since the seed, mass, or lump from which *Adam* was created was somewhat infected with the corrupt disease or malady of the Devil, *Adam* therefore longed for his mother—meaning, he desired to eat of the fruit of the corrupted Earth. At that time, in its outward, physical form, the Earth had become evil, and through the wrath-fire <note>original: wrath-fire; Böhme’s term for the harsh, consuming, or dark aspect of divine power in nature</note>, it had become hard, tangible, and material.

21. Because *Adam’s* spirit longed for that fruit, which shared the quality of the corrupted Earth, Nature formed or shaped such a tree for him that was like the corrupted Earth itself.

22. For *Adam* was the heart of Nature, and therefore his living (or foolish) spirit helped to imagine and shape <term>Image fashion: to bring into physical form through the power of desire or imagination</term> *this tree*, from which he would gladly eat.

23. But when the Devil saw that the desire was in *Adam*, then he struck sharply and briskly at the *Salitter* <term>Salitter: a term used by Böhme to describe the essential divine substance or "salt-nitre" of nature that contains all its creative powers</term> within *Adam*. He infected the *Salitter* from which *Adam* was made even more.

24. And so, it was then time for the Creator to fashion a wife for him, who afterward put the *sin into action* <note>original: "set the Sinne on work"</note> and ate of the false, evil, or corrupt fruit. Otherwise, if *Adam* had eaten of the tree before the woman had been made from him, the situation would have been far worse than it is.

25. But since this requires a high and deep description, as well as a great deal of space, look for the section concerning the *Fall of Adam*, where you will find it described at length.

*So, now I return to the previously mentioned comparison.* <note>original: Similitude</note>

### This is a great Mystery

101. Pay attention here to the sense and meaning: if you understand it, then you understand the Deity correctly; if not, then you are still blind in the *Spirit*.

102. **Do not judge**, otherwise you will run headlong against a strong gate and be imprisoned. If the fire of wrath catches you, then you will remain in it eternally.

103. You child of humanity: see now what a great *Gate* of Heaven, of Hell, and of the Earth—as well as of the entire Deity—the spirit opens for you.

104. You should *not* think that *God* spoke at that time in the same way that humans do, or that it was merely a weak, powerless word like a *human* word.

105. Indeed, a human word forms itself in exactly that same shape, manner, proportion, quality, and correspondence; only a "half-dead" person <note>Boehme often refers to those without spiritual awakening as "half-dead" or "spiritually asleep."</note> does not understand it. 107. It forms and conceives itself first between the teeth when they are closed or pressed together, and it hisses. 33. That is to say, the outermost birth or <term>geniture</term> of this world cannot grasp the outermost birth or <term>geniture</term> of the Heaven *above* this world. They relate to each other like life and death, or like a *man* and a *stone* relate to one another.

34. This world is so securely locked away by it that the outermost birth of the *upper* Heaven cannot enter the outermost birth of this world; there is a great chasm or gulf between them. Therefore, in our physical or outermost birth or <term>geniture</term>, we cannot see the angels. Neither can the angels live with us in the outermost birth of this world, though they do dwell with us in the *innermost* <note>The author suggests that while angels are invisible to our physical senses, they are present within the internal, spiritual essence of humanity</note> part of our being.

### *Concerning the Constitution and form of the*
# Earth.

67. Many authors have written that heaven and earth were created out of NOTHING: but I wonder that among so many excellent men, *not even one* has been found who could yet describe the true foundation <note>original: "true Ground"</note>; seeing that the same God who now is *has been from eternity*.

68. Now, where there is nothing, nothing can come to be: All things *must have a root*, otherwise nothing can grow. If the *seven spirits of nature* <note>Böhme's concept of the seven qualities or "source-spirits" that constitute both the divine nature and the created world.</note> had not been from eternity, then no angel, no heaven, and also no earth would have come to exist.

69. And on the other side, you must also say that there is a *life* within them; otherwise, neither gold nor silver, nor any plant, herb, grass, or vegetable could grow within them.

70. Yes: Life presses through death. The outermost birth is death; the second is Life, which exists within both the wrath-fire <note>The "wrath-fire" refers to the harsh, consuming aspect of divine energy in Boehme's theology, contrasted here with divine Love.</note> and Love; and the *third* is the Holy Life.

71. The outward earth is a bitter stench and is dead; every person understands this to be true. But the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Boehme uses this term to describe the fundamental spiritual-chemical substance or "divine sap" of the universe.</note> is destroyed or killed through death. If you were to say that God created them this way on purpose, it would be the same as saying that God himself is evil, malicious, or wicked.

# Chapter XIX. Concerning the Form of the Earth and the Water, etc.

99. The writer **Moses** says in **Genesis 1**: God separated the **Light** from the **Darkness**, and called the **Light Day**, and the **Darkness, Night**; so from **Evening** and **Morning**, the first **Day** came to be.

100. But since these words—**Evening** and **Morning**—are contrary to the principles of philosophy and logic, it can be understood that **Moses** was not the sole original author of this account. Instead, it was passed down to him from his ancestors, who calculated **all six** days of the Creation in one continuous course. They preserved the memory of the Creation from the time of **Adam** in an obscure word <note>original: "obscure word"; likely referring to a symbolic or esoteric oral tradition</note>, and so left it to posterity.

It is the same with *man* when he kindles the resting wrath-fire, which is otherwise at *rest*.

### *Note.*

**I**t is necessary for the reader to peruse the *Book of the Three Principles* and the *Book of the Threefold Life of Man* along with *this* one; and then he will be able to conceive rightly of the foundation <note>original: "Ground," a technical term in Boehme's theosophy referring to the underlying reality or basis of existence</note> in *this book*, **Aurora**.

For *since* the time of the writing of *this book*, **Aurora**, **Day-spring**, or **Morning Redness**, the lovely *Bright Day* has appeared to the author. And *all* that which is too obscure here is presented *most clearly* in them; which is truly a great **WONDER**, as the reader who loves **God** will find.

Although the author indeed had written this book only *for himself*, according to the gift of **God's** Spirit, he did not know *then* the counsel or will of **God** concerning it.

**T**he *books of this author, which have already been published, sufficiently demonstrate the high worth of his profound writings. Among all the benefits that result from them, one priceless quality is that they help the minds of all kinds of people (who will take the effort to read and consider them) to understand the Holy Scriptures. *And can there be anything more useful, beneficial, necessary, and worthy than this?*

Furthermore, through his writings we may come to understand **how** Christ is the Savior of **all** men, and yet all will not attain salvation. It must be confessed and granted that eternal salvation is attained by some infants, as well as by some innocent, uneducated <note>original: "ignorant"</note> persons of mature years who have been born of Heathen, Jewish, and Christian parents. These are people who have served God according to the law of their forefathers with an upright conscience, such as Paul (who was a Jew), the Eunuch who was a servant to Candace, Queen of Ethiopia (a stranger), and Cornelius the Centurion. All others who fear God and work for righteousness in every nation are accepted by Him, even if they knew nothing of the "great and common salvation" <note>A reference to the idea that God's grace is available to everyone, even those without formal knowledge of the Christian Gospel.</note> that has appeared to all men, as the Apostles knew it.

For if anyone is cleansed from his sins, it is done by the

## **blood of JESUS CHRIST**

which cleanses us from all sin. This is performed in us and for us even when we did not know it, and even though we do not understand how it is done in the slightest, in order to satisfy a soul so that it may be undoubtedly convinced of it.

# Preface to the Reader.

Love God, though few people here in this world truly know anything about him. Yet, he will certainly reveal these things to us on that Day which he has appointed. That day will surely come, though no one knows when it will be or what it will bring, except for the person to whom God reveals it.

Indeed, the writings of people whose understandings have been filled with *spiritual, divine wisdom* are to be valued above all others.

<margin>
Romans 15:4.

Although it is an immense happiness and joy to us that God gave such a vast understanding to those who wrote the Scriptures—and therefore we should read them diligently and frequently while considering them deeply—most of the mysteries within them remain very dark to us. This is because we have so little knowledge of the things the Bible speaks about. Therefore, out of a great love for the Scriptures, how highly should we value and respect the writings of this author, *Jacob Boehme* <note>original: "Jacob Behme"; a German Christian mystic (1575–1624) whose complex works sought to explain the nature of God and the origin of evil.</note>? 

His works disclose the very things that are only briefly hinted at in the Bible. He explains them so fundamentally that he satisfies all the objections that human reason can make. His writings also guide us plainly on the way to find that infallible conductor, the *Holy Spirit*, who will open our minds to discern those hidden mysteries mentioned in the Scriptures so long ago. Thus, through patience and the comfort found in them, we might have hope. Yet, these things were left obscure on purpose, so that some things should be kept secret from the beginning of the world. They were not to be revealed until the proper time and season in every age, and some not until this last age, which is appointed for the manifestation of all mysteries.

### Preface to the Reader.

...**succinct terms** very deeply expressed; but in this [book], the **foundation** of those **terms** is largely and plainly described. It follows the style of the **infancy** of his high **manifestation** <note>This refers to the author's early spiritual revelations or insights.</note> in a **childlike** way, so that it is a large and most clear **ABC** <note>A primer or basic introduction.</note>. It is better suited and plainer for **beginners**, allowing his other books to be more easily understood. This work serves as a **summary of the contents** of all his **mysteries**, and may serve instead of a **manuduction** <term>original: "Manuduction"; a formal word for a guide or manual that "leads one by the hand."</term>, **introduction**, and **key** to unlock all the difficult expressions in his other **books**.

This is because it explains the first **foundation** concerning the **Seven Properties** of the **Eternal Nature**, which he here calls the **Seven Qualifying**, or **fountain spirits** or **qualities**. These are the **Seven Spirits of God**, existing in, from, and to **all eternity**. This edition includes **notes of reference** to the *Book of the Three Principles* and the *Threefold Life of Man*, which compensate for the fact that this **book** was never fully finished. 

The author wrote these notes down with his own hand in their several proper places as expositions in a manuscript belonging to **Michael von Enderns**. His own original **copy** was kept from him by **Gregory Richter**, the **Superintendent** at **Görlitz** <note>original: "Gerlitz"; Richter was a primary antagonist of Boehme who sought to suppress his writings.</note>. That version was **published in print** in **German** <note>original: "high Dutch"; at this time, this term usually referred to German (Hochdeutsch).</note> in 1634, but with many whole verses, lines, and words left out. However, these **notes** were added by the **author** in the year 1620 and are inserted here with **alphabetical marks** in this English translation. 

This translation is made from a **copy** taken from his own handwriting, which was kept hidden for 27 years until November 26, 1641. At that time, it was brought to light by **D.P.S.**, a **Burgomaster** at **Görlitz**, and presented to **George Pflugen**, the **Marshal of the Household** for the **Prince Elector of Saxony** in **Dresden**. # J. B. Preface for the *Aurora*.

## *To the Courteous Reader.*

->I.<-

1. **C** *ourteous Reader*, I compare the whole of *Philosophy*, *Astrology*, and *Theology*, together with their *Mother* <note>The "Mother" refers to Nature or the divine source from which these disciplines spring.</note>, to a beautiful *Tree* which grows in a fair *Garden* of pleasure.

2. Now the *Earth* in which the *Tree* stands provides sap continually to the tree, by which the tree has its living *Quality* <term>original: "Quality" (Quellgeister); in Boehme's thought, this refers to the fundamental forces or driving spirits of being.</term>. But the tree itself grows from the *Sap* of the earth, becomes *Large*, and spreads itself out with its branches. And then, as the *Earth* works with its power upon the tree to make it grow and increase, so the *Tree* also works continually with its branches and all its strength, so that it might still bear good fruit abundantly.

3. But when the *Tree* bears little fruit—and only small, shriveled, rotten, and worm-eaten ones at that—the fault does not lie in the will of the tree, as if it purposefully desired to bear evil fruit, because it is a beautiful *Tree* of good *Quality*. Instead, the fault lies here: because great cold, great heat, mildew, caterpillars, and other worms often happen to it. For the *Quality* in the *Deep* <note>original: "the Deep"; refers to the cosmic expanse or the spiritual atmosphere influenced by the heavens.</note>, coming from the influence of the *Stars*, spoils it, and that makes it bear only a little good fruit.

4. Now the *Tree* is of this nature: the bigger and older it is, the sweeter the fruit it bears. In its younger years it bears little fruit, which the crude and [catchword: wild]

<summary>In this preface, Jacob Boehme introduces an allegory comparing the disciplines of philosophy, astrology, and theology to a tree growing in a garden, sustained by the earth but subject to the influences of the stars and the environment.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Aurora, Philosophy, Astrology, Theology, Nature, Tree of Knowledge, Quality, celestial influence</keywords>

--- Page 330 ---
<meta>This page continues the preface by Jacob Boehme, further developing his "similitude" or analogy of a tree to explain the relationship between God, Nature, and Humanity.</meta>

# J. B. Preface for the Aurora.

[This is what] the wild nature of the ground or earth causes, as does the superfluous <note>original: "superfluous" - here meaning excessive or overflowing</note> moisture in the tree. And though it bears many and beautiful blossoms, yet most of its apples fall off while they are growing; this is not the case when it stands in a very good soil or earth. Now this tree also has a good, sweet quality, but there are three others which are contrary to it: namely, the bitter, the sour, and the astringent <term>astringent: a harsh, drying, or contracting taste, often associated in Boehme’s thought with the "contracting" force of nature</term>.

5. And as the tree is, so will its fruit be, until the Sun works on them and makes them sweet, so that they acquire a sweet taste; its fruit must also hold out through rain, wind, and tempest.

6. But when the tree grows old, so that its branches wither and the sap ascends *no more*, then below the stem or stock many suckers grow; at last, twigs grow from the root as well and make the old tree flourish, showing that *it* also was once a green twig and a young tree, and has now become old. For *Nature*, or the sap, struggles until the stock grows quite dry, and then it is to be cut down and burnt in the fire.

7. Now observe what I have signified by this <term>similitude: an extended metaphor or analogy</term>: the Garden of this tree signifies the *World*; the soil or earth signifies *Nature*; the stock of the tree signifies the *Stars*; by the branches are meant the *Elements*; the fruit which grows on this tree signifies *Mankind*; the sap in the tree resembles the pure *Deity*. Now *Mankind* was made out of *Nature*, the *Stars*, and the *Elements*, but God the Creator reigns in all—even as the sap does in the whole tree.

8. But there are two *Qualities in Nature*, even until the *Judgment of God*: the one is pleasant, heavenly, and holy; the other is fierce, wrathful, hellish, and thirsty.

<summary>Boehme provides an allegorical interpretation of a tree, where the sap represents the Deity and the fruit represents Mankind, illustrating how God reigns through all elements of the natural world. He introduces the concept of dual qualities in nature—one holy and one wrathful—which persist until the final Judgment.</summary>

<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Aurora, allegory, Nature, Deity, Elements, Stars, Mankind, dualism, spiritual qualities</keywords>

--- Page 331 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's preface to the Aurora, further exploring the duality of good and evil within nature and humanity.</meta>

<page-num>3</page-num>
-> J. B. Preface for the Aurora. <-
<sig>B 2</sig>

9. Now the good quality operates <note>original: "qualifieth"; in Böhme's writing, this refers to how a substance acts or interacts according to its essential nature</note> and works continually with all industry to bring forth good fruit, and the *Holy Ghost* reigns therein and affords to it sap and life. The bad quality springs and drives with all its endeavor to bring forth *bad* fruit continually, to which the devil affords sap and *hellish* flame. Now both are in the tree of Nature, and *Men* are made out of that tree and live in this world—in this garden—between both, in great danger. Suddenly the Sun shines on them; soon after, winds, rain, and snow fall on them.

10. That is: if man elevates his spirit into the *Deity*, then the *Holy Ghost* moves, springs, and operates in him. But if he permits his spirit to sink into the world, in lust toward *evil*, then the *Devil* and hellish sap stir and reign in him.

11. Just as the *Apple* on the tree becomes corrupt, rotten, and worm-eaten when frost, heat, and mildew fall on it, and easily falls off and perishes; so does Man also when he suffers the *Devil* to rule in him with his *poison*.

12. Now, just as there is, springs, and reigns both good and bad in Nature, even so it is in Man. Though evil sticks to him—just as in *Nature* the evil hangs on the good—yet he can overcome the evil if he elevates his spirit in God; for then the *Holy Ghost* stirs and moves in him, and helps him to overcome.

The South <note>original: "South" — Likely a reference to a specific spiritual or geopolitical direction in Boehme’s complex mystical cosmology.</note> made an assault upon them: then the holy people flourished greatly in their blossom, just as it was in the beginning when the holy and precious tree grew and overcame the wrath or fierceness in Nature and its ruler; thus it was at that time.

50. Now, when the noble and holy Tree was revealed *to all nations*, so that they saw how it moved over them and spread its fragrance over all people, and that anyone who pleased might eat of it; then the people grew weary of eating its *fruit* which grew on the tree, and longed to eat of the *Root of the Tree*. The cunning and wise people sought after the *Root* and argued about it. So, the strife was great regarding the root of the tree, to the point that they forgot to eat of the fruit of the sweet tree because of the *controversy* about the root of the tree.

51. And now they cared for *neither* the Root nor the Tree, but the prince of darkness <note>prince of darkness: Satan or the personification of evil.</note> had another design, intending something else. When he saw that they would eat no more of the good Tree but argued about the Root, he perceived that they had grown *very weak and faint*, and that wild Nature predominated in them again;

52. And therefore he incited them to pride, so that everyone supposed he had the Root at hand—that everyone must look to him, hear him, and honor him. By this, they built their palaces and great houses and secretly served their idol *Mammon* <note>Mammon: A biblical term for wealth or material greed, often personified as a false god.</note>. Because of this, the common <note>original: "Lay"</note> people were troubled and led to sin, and so lived in physical <note>original: "carnal"</note> pleasures according to the desires of *wild* Nature, and served their bellies in self-indulgence <note>original: "wantonnesse"</note>, relying on the fruit of the tree which moved over them all, thinking that even if they fell into misery, they might be healed by it.

53. In the meantime, they served the prince of darkness according to the impulses of their wild nature, and the precious tree stood there only as a <term>May-game</term><note>original: "May-game"; an object of ridicule, sport, or a frivolous distraction</note> or mocking stock. Many lived like *wild beasts* and led wicked lives in pride, pomp, vanity, and lust—the rich consuming the labor and sweat of the poor and forcing them into such a state.

54. All evil actions were excused through bribery. The *laws* emerged out of the evil <gloss>quality</gloss><note>In Boehme’s writing, "quality" refers to the essential forces or properties of nature, whether divine or wrathful</note> of nature, and everyone strove after *riches* and goods, pride, pomp, and status. There was *no* savior for the poor. Verbal abuse, insults, cursing, and swearing were *not* condemned nor seen as vicious; thus, people defiled themselves in a wrathful or fierce *nature*, just as a pig wallows in the dirt and mire.

55. The shepherds <note>Meaning the religious leaders or clergy</note> treated the sheep <note>The common people or their congregations</note> this way; they kept nothing but the bare *name* of the noble tree. Its fruit, virtue, and life were used only as a cover for their *sins*. This is how the world lived at that time, except for a small remnant or number of people who were born in the midst of "thorns" <note>A biblical metaphor for the righteous living among the wicked</note> in great *tribulation* and contempt, out of all nations upon the earth, from the East to the West.

56. There was no difference; they all lived upon the impulse of their wild nature in *weakness*, except for a small number who were delivered out of all nations. It was as it had been before the <term>Deluge</term><note>The Great Flood of Noah</note> and before the noble tree grew in nature; it was just the same at that time.

57. But why men, in the end, longed so eagerly for the root of the tree is a *mystery*, and until now it was hidden from the "wise and prudent." Neither will it rise up to the heights <note>The heights of intellectual pride or worldly status</note>, but only in the "Deep" <note>Boehme’s term for the divine essence found in humility</note>, in great simplicity.

58. As indeed the noble tree, with its kernel and heart, has *always* been concealed from those who are worldly-wise; though they supposed they stood, some at the root and some at the very top of the tree, yet this was no more than a shining mist before their eyes.

59. But from the beginning until now, the noble tree strove within Nature to its utmost so that it might be revealed to *all people*, tongues, and languages. Against this, the Devil, in his wild nature, raged and fought like a fierce lion.

60. But the noble tree bore more and sweeter fruit, and revealed itself more and more against all the fury and madness of the Devil, even unto the end; and then *it was light. For a green twig grew at the root of the noble tree, which received the sap and life of the root, and to which the Spirit of the tree was given. So it increased and multiplied the noble tree in its glorious virtue <note>original: "vertue"; in this context, it refers to the inherent power or divine efficacy of the tree.</note> and power, and also in the nature in which it grew.*

61. Now when this was done, then *both the gates of Nature were opened—the knowledge of the two qualities of good and evil—and so the Heavenly Jerusalem <note>Boehme uses this term to describe the spiritual state of divine peace, light, and harmony.</note> was manifested, as was the Kingdom of Hell, to all people upon Earth.* And the Light and voice were heard in the *four winds*, and the false merchant in the South <note>Likely a symbolic reference to the Papacy or the institutional Church of Rome, which Boehme and other contemporary reformers often characterized as a corrupt commercial entity.</note> was completely revealed; and his *own* people hated him and rooted him out from the whole earth.

62. This being done, the wild tree toward the North withered, and all people beheld the holy tree with admiration, even in *foreign islands*. And the Prince in the darkness <note>original: "Prince in the darkneſſe"; a traditional title for Satan.</note> was revealed, and his mysteries were discovered, along with his shame, disgrace, and destruction. The people upon earth did see and *know* this, for it was *Light*.

63. And this lasted only a short time, for men abandoned that light and lived in carnal pleasures to their own destruction <note>original: "perdition"</note>. For as the gate of light had opened itself, so also did the gate of darkness; and from them both emerged all kinds of powers and arts that were contained within them.

64. For as men had lived from the beginning in the growth of wild nature and hunted only after earthly things, so in the end, things were not improved but rather grew worse.

65. During the middle of this time, many great, stormy winds were raised from the West toward the East and North. But from the North, a great *stream of water* went forth toward the holy tree, and *in the midst of the stream, there was light*; and so the wild tree toward the North withered.

66. And then the Prince in the darkness <note>Boehme often refers to Lucifer or a personified spirit of evil as the "Prince of Darkness."</note> was enraged by the great movement of Nature. For the *Holy Tree* moved in Nature, like one that would soon be elevated and kindled <note>original: "kindled"; in Boehme's writing, this refers to being ignited or activated by spiritual life or fire</note> in the glorification of the holy *Divine Majesty*. It cast away the wrath <note>original: "wrath or fierceness"</note> that had stood against it and wrestled with it for so long.

67. In the same way, the tree of darkness, wrath, fierceness, and destruction moved furiously, like one about to be ignited. And in that moment, the Prince with his *Legions* went forth to spoil the noble fruit of the good tree.

68. And it appeared horrifying in Nature—in that fierce quality <note>Boehme uses "quality" to describe the essential characteristics or spiritual forces of a being or state.</note> where the Prince of Darkness dwelt, to speak in human terms. It was just as when people see a terrible storm approaching, appearing horrible with lightning and tempestuous winds, leaving people standing in amazement.

69. # The Contents of this Book, by way of Introduction.

I have given this book the following name:

## The Root or Mother of **Philosophy**, **Astrology**, and **Theology**.

And so that you may know what this book treats,

->Observe,<-

### I.

1. In the *Philosophy*, <note>original: "Philosophie"</note> the **Divine power** is discussed, specifically:

I. *What* God *is;*
II. *How* Nature, *the* stars, *and the* elements *were created in the Being of* God;
III. *From where everything has its* origin; <note>original: "Original"</note>
IV. *How* heaven *and* earth *were created;*
V. *How* angels, humanity, *and* devils *were created;*
VI. *How* heaven *and* hell, *and whatever is a created thing, were created, and what the* **two qualities** <note>Boehme’s concept of "Qualities" refers to the inherent forces or properties (like light and dark, or heat and cold) that drive all existence.</note> *are in* nature.

All this is drawn from a true foundation in the knowledge of the Spirit, by the impulse and movement of God.

<summary>This page introduces the book's title and outlines the first section on Philosophy, which explores the nature of God, the creation of the cosmos, and the fundamental forces of nature.</summary>

## II.

2. In the *Astrology* <note>In this period, "Astrology" referred more broadly to "natural philosophy" or the study of how celestial and elemental forces influence the physical world.</note>, the following are discussed:
> I. *Of the powers of Nature, of the Stars, and of the Elements.*
> II. *How all Creatures proceeded from these.*
> III. *How these same forces impel and rule all things.*
> IIII. *How they work in all things, and how good and evil are wrought by them in Men and Beasts.*
> V. *From where it comes that Good and Evil exist and reign in this world.*
> VI. *Also how the Kingdom of Heaven and of Hell consist within them.*

3. My purpose is not to describe the course, position, and name of all stars, nor what their annual Conjunction, Opposition, or Square <note>original: "Quadrat"; an astrological aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart, often considered a position of tension.</note> is, or the like; nor what they operate yearly and hourly. Such things have been observed over a long period of time by wise, skillful, and expert men, who were rich and expansive in spirit through their diligent contemplation, observation, deep insight, calculation, and computation.

4. Neither have I studied or learned these things, and I leave it to the scholars to discourse upon them. Instead, my intention is to write according to the Spirit and the senses <gloss>original German: Sinne</gloss>, and not according to intellectual speculation <gloss>original German: Anschauen; here meaning outward observation or sensory intuition</gloss>.

## III.

5. In the *Theology* the following are handled:
> I. *Of the Kingdom of Christ, and what its nature is.*
> II. *How it is set in opposition to the Kingdom of Hell.*

# III. The Stars, the Elements, and the Creatures which have proceeded from them; as also the Holy Angels, Devils, and Men; and furthermore, Heaven and Hell.

## Of the Two Qualities in One.

->3.<-

In this consideration, two qualities are found—a good one and an evil one—which exist within one another as a single thing in this world. They are in all powers, in the stars, and in the elements, as well as in all creatures. No creature in the flesh, in its natural life, can exist <note>original: "fubfift"</note> unless it possesses these two qualities.

## What a * QUALITY is.

<margin>
* The understanding of the thing here called QUALITY is the foundation of the entire revelation of Jacob Boehme <note>original: "Jacob Behme"</note> and of all mysteries, of which his writings are only a description. Throughout his work, the seven qualities are sometimes called seven sources, seven species, kinds, manners, circumstances, conditions, powers, operations, or faculties of a thing. They are also called the Qualifying or Fountain Spirits, which give, model, image, or frame the power, virtue, color, taste, figure, shape, constitution, substance, essence, and distinct being of all things—all things that ever were, are, shall be, or can be, in, from, and to all eternity; in God and all creatures; in heaven, in hell, or in this world. They are also the forms or properties of Nature, which is the *Salitter* <term>Salitter: A term used by Boehme to describe the divine power or "sap" of the universe, analogous to saltpeter or the fundamental substance of God's power.</term> or power of God. And so, they are the seven spirits of God, as mentioned in the Revelation of John, Chapter 1:4, Chapter 3:1, Chapter 4:5, and Chapter 5:6.

A quality is the mobility—the boiling, springing, and driving—of a thing.

# Of the operation of the Cold Quality.

->15:<-

*Cold* is also a quality, just like *Heat*. It operates <term>original: "qualifieth"; here meaning the way a substance acts, exerts influence, or interacts with others</term> in all creatures—whatever comes forth in *Nature*, and in everything that moves within it: in men, beasts, birds <note>original: "fowles"</note>, fishes, worms, leaves, and grass.

16. And Heat is set in *opposition* to it, and operates within it as if they were one and the same thing; however, cold opposes the fierceness or rage of the heat and tempers <note>original: "allayeth"</note> the heat.

17. It also contains two sorts or species within itself, which should be noted: namely, it mitigates the heat and makes all things pleasant. It is a quality of life in all creatures, for no creature can exist without cold; it is a springing, driving mobility <note>the author uses "Mobility" to describe the vital, restless energy or movement inherent in natural forces</note> in everything.

18. The other kind or *species* is *fierceness* <term>In this context, "fierceness" refers to the harsh, destructive, or extreme aspect of a natural force, as opposed to its mild, life-sustaining aspect.</term>. For where it gains power, it suppresses and ruins <note>original: "spoileth"</note> everything, just as the heat does. No life can survive in it if the heat did not prevent that. The fierceness of cold is the destruction of every life and the house of death, just as the fierceness of heat is.

### Of the Divine Being in Nature, and Chapter 1.

## Of the Sweet Quality.

->34.<-

The *Sweet Quality* is set opposite to the *Bitter* and is a gracious, amiable, blessed, and pleasant quality. It is a refreshing of life and an allaying <note>allaying: soothing or moderating</note> of fierceness; it makes everything pleasant and friendly in every creature. It makes the *plants* <note>original: "Vegetables"</note> of the *Earth* fragrant and good-tasting, producing beautiful yellow, white, and ruddy *colors*.

35. It is a glimpse and source of *meekness*, a pleasant habitation of heavenly joyfulness, a house or mansion of the *Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>, a manifestation <note>original: "qualification"</note> of *love* and *mercy*, and a joy of life.

36. But on the other hand, it also has a fierce or wrathful source—a source of death and corruption. For if it is kindled in the *bitter quality* within the *element of water*, then it breeds diseases, the "botchy" plague <note>likely referring to bubonic plague, characterized by "botches" or sores</note> or pestilence, and the corruption of the flesh.

37. But if it is kindled in heat and bitterness, then it infects the *element of air*, which engenders a sudden spreading plague and sudden death.

# Of the Sour Quality.

->38.<-

The *Sour Quality* <note>original: "Soure Quality"; in Boehme’s thought, this is the first of the seven "source-spirits," representing a contracting, attracting force</note> is set in opposition to the Bitter and the Sweet, and is a beneficial tempering force to all things. It provides refreshing and cooling when the bitter and sweet qualities are too highly elevated. It is a longing delight in the taste, a pleasure of life, and a stirring, boiling, flowing joy in everything; it is a desire, longing, and lust for joyfulness—a quiet joy or a dwelling place for the *Spirit*. Thus, it acts as a balancing influence for all living and moving creatures.

**A**ll that has been mentioned above is therefore called *Quality*, because it qualifies, operates, or frames everything in the Deep <note>original: "the Deepe"; the vast celestial space or the abyss of the cosmos</note> above the earth, as well as upon the earth and in the earth—working in one another as *ONE* thing. Yet it has several distinct virtues <note>original: "vertues"; inherent powers or properties</note> and operations, and but one mother from whom all things descend and spring.

2. And all creatures are made and descended from these *qualities*, and live within them as if in their mother. # Chap. II. Further of the Two Qualities.

->*Now observe here further:*<-

->46.<-

The whole body, up to the neck, signifies and is the round circle or sphere of the stars, as well as the deep <note>Original: "the Deep" (the vast, underlying abyss or space of the universe)</note> within or between the stars, where the *planets* and *elements* reign.

47. The *flesh* signifies the earth, which is congealed <note>Original: "congealed" (solidified or hardened into matter)</note> and has no motion of its own. 48. The earth could no more bring forth any fruit, nor could any metals grow—such as gold, silver, copper, iron, or stones—if the *stars* did not work within them; neither could any grass grow without the operation of the *stars*.

49. The *head* signifies heaven. It has grown upon the body through the veins, passages, and the outgoing of powers; in the same way, all powers return from the head and *brain* into the body, into the source-veins <note>Original: "fountain-veins" (referring to the arteries or vital channels through which life-force flows)</note> or arteries of the flesh.

50. Now, heaven is a pleasant palace of joy, where all the powers exist just as they do in the whole of nature within the *stars* and elements, but they are not so harshly active or forceful. For every power of *heaven* has only one species, kind, or form of power, springing forth very brightly and gently—not mixed with good and evil together as in the stars and elements, but remaining very pure.

51. It is made out of the midst of the waters, but it does not "quality" <note>Original: "qualifying" (Boehme’s technical term for how various forces or "qualities" interact, influence, and manifest within one another)</note> in the same way as the water in the elements, for no fierceness or wrath is found there. However, heaven belongs to nature because the stars and elements have their origin and power from *heaven*.

### Question.

Here now the question is: From where does Heaven get, or from where does it borrow, this power that causes such *mobility* in nature?

### Answer.

59. Here you must lift up your eyes beyond nature, into the light-holy triumphing divine power—into the unchangeable Holy Trinity, which is a triumphing, springing, movable Being; all powers are within it, just as they are in nature.

60. For this is the *Eternal Mother* of nature, from which heaven, earth, stars, elements, angels, devils, humans, beasts, and all things have their being; everything exists within it.

61. When we name heaven and earth, stars and elements, and all that is within them—and everything whatsoever that is above the heavens—then we are naming the *Total God*. He has made himself *creaturely* <note>original: "Creaturely"; meaning God has manifested himself in the form of created beings and physical matter.</note> in these beings mentioned above, through his power which goes forth from him.

62. But God in his Trinity is unchangeable, and whatever there is in heaven and upon earth, and above the earth, has its spring, source, and origin from the *power* which proceeds from God.

63. Yet you must *not* therefore imagine that in God there is both good and evil; for God himself is the *Good*, and he takes his *name* from "good," <note>The author is highlighting the linguistic connection between the words "God" and "good."</note> which is the triumphing eternal joy. However, *all the powers* proceed from him—those which you can search out in nature, and those which are in all things.
