lasting power, in an elevating, triumphing spring or source of joy.

72. And though it is written in *Moses*, "*I am an angry, jealous God*" (Exodus 20; Deuteronomy 4:24), the meaning of it is *not* that God is angry *within himself*, or that a fire of anger arises within the *Holy Trinity*. <note>original: "zealous"; in this context, it refers to the biblical description of God as "jealous" for His people's devotion.</note>

73. No, that cannot be; for it is written, "*against those that hate me*." It is within that same creature <note>A "creature" refers to any created being, such as a human or an angel.</note> that the fire of anger rises up.

74. If God were to be angry within himself, then all of *nature* would be on fire. This will happen once *on the Last Day within nature*, but *not within God*. Instead, *within God, the triumphing joy will burn*. It was never otherwise from eternity, nor will it ever be otherwise.

75. Now, this elevating, springing, triumphing joy in God makes heaven triumphant and movable; and heaven makes the stars and elements movable; and the stars and the elements make the *crearies* movable.

76. Out of the *powers of God*, the heavens have proceeded; out of *heaven* came the stars; out of the stars came the elements; and out of the *elements*, the *earth* and the *creatures* have come to be.

## Of the Holy TRINITY.

80. Now when we speak or write of the *three persons* in the Godhead, you must not *imagine* <note>original: "conceive."</note> that there are therefore three Gods, each reigning and ruling by himself like earthly <note>original: "temporal."</note> kings on the earth.

<margin>Or, the Trinity has no such physical substance and being in God.</margin>
81. No: such a substance and being is not in God; for the divine *being* consists in power and not in a physical body or flesh.

82. The Father is the entire divine power, from which *all creatures* <note>original: "creatures" here refers to all created things, not just animals.</note> have come forth, and He has always been from eternity; He has neither beginning nor end.

83. The Son is in the Father, being the Father's heart or light; and the Father generates the Son continually from eternity to eternity. The Son’s power and splendor shine back again throughout the whole Father, just as the *sun* does in the whole world.

84. Also, the Son is *another* person than the Father, but not externally outside of or severed from the Father; *nor* is he any other God than the Father is.

43. But nature has *not* been able to produce heavenly power, virtue, and qualities; therefore, its fruit is half-dead, corrupt, and impure.

60. As I have shown *before*, there are two things especially to be observed in the "Deep" <note>original: "Deep"; referring to the infinite, unmanifested essence of God</note> of God the Father: first, the power—or rather all powers—of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost are very lovely, pleasant, and diverse; yet they are all *within one another* as a single power.

61. And just as the powers of all the stars rule in the air, so they do in God. However, every power in God *reveals itself through its own operation*, individually and distinctly.

62. Then afterward, the Sound exists in every power, and the tone or tune of that Sound corresponds to the quality of each power. Within this consists the entire Heavenly Kingdom of Joy. Thus, from this divine *Salitter* <note>original: "Salitter"; a term used by the author to describe the divine substance or "salt-nitre" of the heavenly realm</note> and *Mercurius* <note>original: "Mercurius"; representing the active, moving principle or "spirit" within the divine substance</note>, all angels are made—that is, out of the "Body of Nature."

## Of the Qualification of an Angel.

->*Question.*<-

35. The *question* now is: What kind of *qualification* <note>original: "qualification"; in this context, it refers to the innate properties, sensory powers, or the way a being interacts with its environment</note> does an *angel* have?

->*Answer.*<-

36. The *holy soul* of a man and the *spirit* of an *angel* are and have one and the same *substance* and *being*. There is no difference between them except in the *quality* itself, or their corporeal <term>bodily</term> government. In man, that which *qualifies outwardly* (or from the outside) through the *air* has a *corrupt earthly* quality. Yet, on the other hand, it also has a *divine* and *heavenly* quality that is hidden from created *beings*.

37. But the holy soul understands this well, as the royal prophet *David* says: "*The Lord rides on the wings of the wind*" (*Psalm 104:3*).

->*Question.*<-

38. But a simple person may ask: What do you mean by the word *qualifying*, or what is that?

->*Answer.*<-

39. By that, I mean the power which *enters into* the *body* of the *angel* from the outside and comes out again. To use a *similitude* <term>comparison or analogy</term>: it is like when a man draws a breath and breathes it out again; for in that process lies the life of both the *body* and the *spirit*.

# The Sixth Chapter.

->*How an Angel and a Man are the Likeness and Image of God.*<-

->1.<-

**B**ehold! Just as the *essence* <note>original: "Being". Therefore, it is fitting that they should be in *subjection* to the whole essence, seeing as they are the *son of its body*.

3. Now, if the *son* resists and *opposes* the *Father*, it is only right that the *Father* should cast him out of the *House*, since the *son* sets himself against the one who generated him and from whose power he became a creature.

4. For if anyone makes something out of what is his own, he may—if it does *not* turn out according to his will—do with it as he pleases, *and make it either a vessel of honor or dishonor*; which is exactly what happened to *Lucifer*.

->*Now Observe:*<-

...such a substance. Indeed, it is most certain and true that *there are all manner of fruits in heaven*, and they are *not* merely types and shadows. Also, the angels *pluck* them with their hands and eat them just as we humans do. However, they do *not* need any teeth to do it with, *nor do they have any*, for the fruit consists of a divine power.

30. Now all of this—whatever an angel makes use of that is externally *outside* of him to support his life—is *not* his corporal property <term>original: "propriety," meaning legal ownership or personal possession</term>, as if he held it by a *natural right*. Rather, the *Heavenly Father* gives it to them in love.

31. It is true that their body is their own property, for God has given it to them as a possession. Now, whatever is given to anyone as his *own* or as property belongs to him by *right of nature*; a person does not act righteously if he takes it away from him again, unless it is by condition or agreement. God does *not* do this either; therefore, an angel is an eternal, incorruptible creature who stands or subsists throughout all eternity.

32. But what would the body benefit him if God did *not* feed it? For then it would have no mobility and would lie still like a dead block. *Therefore*, the angels are obedient to God and humble themselves before the powerful God. They honor, laud, and praise Him for His great deeds and works of wonder, and they sing continually of God's *holiness*, *because* He feeds them.

# The Eighth Chapter.

->Concerning the whole *Body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> or Body of an *Angelic Kingdom*.<-

## *The Great Mystery.*

->I.<-

**T**he Angelic Kingdoms are formed *entirely* according to the Divine Being, and they have no other form or *condition* than that which the *Divine Being* has in its Trinity.

2. The only difference is this: their bodies are *created beings* <note>In this context, "creature" refers to any created thing, distinct from the uncreated God.</note> which have a beginning and an end. Furthermore, the kingdom where their location, *habitation*, or court is situated is not their own physical property <note>original: "corporeal propriety"</note>; they do not possess it by natural right as they possess their bodies by a *natural* right.

3. Instead, the kingdom belongs to God the Father, who has made it out of his powers, and he may establish and *arrange* <note>original: "dispose"</note> it in whatever way he pleases. Otherwise, their body is made according to all, and out of all, the *powers* of the Father.

4. And their power generates light and knowledge *within them*. Just as God generates his Son out of *all his powers*, and just as the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> goes forth from all the powers of the Father and the Son, so also in an angel, the spirit goes forth from their heart, from their light, and from all their powers.

# I.
## *On the First Type or Circumstance.*

22. First, within the hidden, secret Divine power, there is the **astringent quality**. This coldness is very sharp, like salt, and is very hard, binding, knitting, and pulling things together like a stone.

# Of the Second Species or Circumstance.

->32.<-

The *second quality* or *second spirit* of God in the *divine Salitter* <term>Salitter: A term used by Boehme to describe the fundamental divine substance or "spiritual earth" of the heavenly realm</term>, or in the *divine power*, is the *sweet quality*. 35. 38. Thus, the astringent quality is—and is called—the Heart; and the sweet quality is called *Barm*, or *warm*, or softening, or *mitigating*. These are the two qualities from which the Heart, or the Son of God, is generated.

# IV.
# Of the Fourth Circumstance or Category <note>original: "Species"</note>

59.
The fourth Quality, or the fourth source-spirit <note>original: "fountain-Spirit"</note> in the Divine power of God the Father, is Heat, which is the true *Beginning of life*, and also the true *Spirit of Life*.

60. The astringent <term>harsh or contracting</term>, sour, and sweet quality is the *Salitter* <term>a term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of the spiritual world</term>, which belongs to the *Body* and out of which the *Body* is framed.

61. For coldness and hardness reside in the *astringent quality*, and consist of *contraction* and *drying*; and in the *sweet quality* reside the *water*, the *light* or *radiance* <note>original: "shiningnesse"</note>, and the entire matter of the *Body*.

62. And the *bitter quality* is the *separation* and *forming*, and the *Heat* is the *Spirit* or the *kindling* of *life*, by which the *Spirit* exists in the *Body*. This Spirit springs or moves within the whole *Body* and shines out from the *Body*; it also creates the *living motion* in all the qualities of the *Body*.

63. Two things are chiefly to be observed in all the *qualities*: if you look upon a *Body*, you see first the *core essence* <note>original: "Stock Pith"</note> or the *Kernel* of all the *qualities*, which is framed or *composed* out of all the *qualities*. For to the *Body* belong the astringent <term>harsh</term>, sour, sweet, bitter, and hot qualities; these qualities, being dried together, make the *Body* or *trunk* <note>original: "Stock"</note>.

# The Ninth Chapter.

## Of the Gracious, *Amiable, Blessed, Friendly, and* Merciful Love of God.

### The Great Heavenly and Divine *Mystery*.

->I.<-

**B**ecause I write here of heavenly and divine things, which are altogether strange to the corrupted, perished nature of man, the reader will no doubt wonder at the *simplicity* <note>original: "simplicity"; here meaning a lack of worldly sophistication or a plain, unadorned style</note> of the author and be offended by it.

2. This is because the condition and inclination of our corrupted nature is to gaze *only* on *high* things—like a proud, wild, wanton, and *unfaithful* <note>original: "whorish"</note> woman, who always gazes in her heat or burning lust after *handsome* men to act wantonly with them.

3. So it is with the proud, corrupted, and perished nature of man: it stares only upon *that* which is glittering and *fashionable* in this world, and supposes that God has forgotten the afflicted, and therefore plagues them because he does not care for them <note>original: "mindeth them not"</note>.

4. Corrupt nature imagines that the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> regards only *high* things: the advanced arts and sciences of *this world*, profound studies, and great learning.

### Of the Nativity and Life of the Holy Angels. Chapter XII.

I. The Stars symbolize or represent the *Angels*: for just as the stars must remain unchanged until the end of time, the *Angels* must also remain unchanged forever in the eternal time of heaven.

166. II. The Elements symbolize or represent the wonderful proportion, variety, change, and alteration of the form and appearance of Heaven. For just as the depths between the stars and Earth always alter and change in their form—at one moment it is fair, bright, and light, and suddenly it is gloomy and dark; now there is wind, then rain; now snow, and suddenly the depths are blue or azure, then greenish, soon after whitish, and then suddenly dark and shadowy again.

167. In this same way, there is change and alteration in Heaven, into many various colors and forms, though not in the same manner or kind as in this world. Instead, all this occurs according to the surging <note>original: "rising up," referring to the dynamic movement of divine forces</note> of the Spirits of God, and the Light of the Son of God shines within it eternally. However, the intensity of this divine generation <note>original: "rising up in the birth"</note> differs in its degrees at certain times more than others.

->***And therefore the wonderful wisdom of God is incomprehensible.***<-

<margin>*</margin>
168. III. The Earth symbolizes or represents the Heavenly Nature, or the "seventh spirit of Nature," in which the ideas, images, forms, and colors arise.

169. IV. *And the birds, fish, and beasts symbolize or represent the various forms or shapes of figures in Heaven.*

You are to know this—for the spirit in the Flash <term>The "Flash" (or *Blitz* in the original German) is a central concept in the writings of mystic Jacob Boehme, referring to the sudden spark of divine illumination or the moment of creation</term> testifies to the same—that in Heaven there arise

->Question.<-

# Listen, Lucifer: Where does the fault lie now, that you have become a devil? Is God at fault, as you lyingly say?

->Answer.<-

58. Oh no, you yourself are at fault. The <term>qualifying spirits</term><note>original: "qualifying or fountain Spirits." In the philosophy of Jakob Böhme, these are the seven core forces or "fountains" that constitute the essence of all beings.</note> in your body, which are your very essence, have generated you as *such* a "little son." You cannot say that God has kindled the <term>Salitter</term><note>A term used by Böhme to describe the divine substance or "spiritual saltpeter" that makes up the heavenly realm.</note> out of which He made you. Instead, your own qualifying spirits have done it, whereas before you were clearly a prince and a king of God.

59. Therefore, when you say God created you this way, or that He has—*without* sufficient cause—expelled you from your place, then you are a liar and a murderer. For the whole heavenly host or army bears witness against you that you yourself have built and prepared this fierce quality for yourself.

60. If it is not so, then go before the face of God and *justify* yourself. But you see the truth clearly enough without doing that; and besides, you do not dare to look upon that matter. Would you not gladly have a friendly kiss from the Son of God, so that you might at last be eased or refreshed? If you are in the right, then just look upon HIM once; perhaps you might be made sound or whole again.

### Answer

125. Now show me any place to which you send your covetous or lustful spirit—whether it be toward man, beasts, garments, fields, money, or anything whatsoever—where God is *not*. Everything comes from him, and he is in everything; he himself is *everything*, and he upholds and supports everything.

### Objection

->Then you will say:<-

# Chapter XV. On Lucifer.

29. For in the sweet water, it is very gentle <note>original: "meek"</note>; from this, Love exists, being only a loving warmth and not a fire.

30. And although it is indeed located within the hidden core <note>original: "kernel"</note> of the fire’s nature <note>original: "quality"</note> or its origin <note>original: "Originall"</note>, that fire is not ignited or burning, because it is generated within the sweet water.

31. Now, wherever the water is present, there is no burning fire, but rather a pleasant warmth and a gentle life-giving <note>original: "qualifying or vivifying"</note> power. However, if the water were to be dried up, then a burning fire would break out there.

32. Lord *Lucifer* thought the same: he believed that if he simply ignited his fire, he could rule by force within the Divine power. He assumed it would burn *eternally* and also provide *light*. His intention was not to extinguish the *light*; rather, he wanted it to burn continuously within the fire. He thought he could dry up the water, and then the light would move, stir, or shine within the burning fire.

33. But he did *not* know that if he ignited the dried water, the core—that is, the oiliness <note>original: "unctuosity"</note>, oil, or heart of the water—would be *consumed*. He did not realize that the light would turn into darkness and the water would turn into a sour stench.

34. For the oil or oiliness in the water is generated through gentleness or goodness. This is the oiliness, oil, anointing <note>original: "unction"</note>, marrow, or richness <note>original: "fatness"</note> in which the *light* shines. But if this oiliness is burnt up, the water turns into a sour stench and, moreover, becomes very dark.

35. And this is what happened to the pride of *Lucifer*. He triumphed for a short time with his ignited *light*; however, when his light was exhausted and burnt away, he became a black devil.

### Of the Sixth Type, Kind, Form, or Manner of Sin’s Beginning in Lucifer and in His Angels.

71. The sixth qualifying or source-spirit in the Divine power is *Mercurius* <note>original: *Mercurius*; in this context, it refers to the principle of sound, motion, and communication</note>, or the Tone or Tune, through which heavenly joy arises.

72. This spirit originates in the "fire-flash"—that is, in the bitter quality—and rises up through the "sweet water" in the flash. There, it softens itself so that it becomes clear and bright, and it is held within the astringent <note>original: *astringent*; the contractive or "harsh" force in nature</note> quality. In that state, it *touches* or stirs all the other spirits, and from this stirring, the Tone arises. Its rising source or quality resides in the flash, but its "body" or root resides in the sweet water of *Love*.

73. Now, this Tone or Tune is the *Divine Joyfulness*, the triumphing state in which the gentle "play of love" <note>original: *Love-play sport or scene*; the harmonious and creative interaction of divine forces</note> in God emerges, along with the formation of all *Ideas*, shapes, and figures.

74. But here you must understand that this quality penetrates all the other spirits very gently and pleasantly as it stirs them. It is like a pleasant and gentle fire of joy rising in a person’s heart; in that fire of joy, the soul’s spirit triumphs as if it were in *Heaven*.

75. This spirit does *not* concern itself with the imaging or framing of the body itself, but rather with the distinction, diversity, and mobility—especially the joy and the specific differences in how shapes and forms are created.

First there is the astringent quality, *then* the sweet, and *next* the bitter. The sweet is in the middle, between the astringent and the bitter. 25. Now, the astringent and bitter qualities, *without* the sweet water, rub and drive themselves *so hard* against one another that they generate dark heat, and so they are kindled within themselves.

## Now Observe:

26. Now, when the fire-spirit and the astringent <note>The quality of contraction or drawing together</note> spirit struggle and wrestle together in this way, the astringent spirit creates a vehement, hard *cold astriction*, and the fiery spirit creates a terrible, fierce *heat*.

29. 64. For *every* spirit among the seven spirits of God is filled with *all* seven spirits; they all exist within one another as *one* spirit, and none of them exists without the others.

## Ch. X. Of the sixth fountain spirit in the Divine Power.

119. For the kindled spirits of God <note>These are the seven "Source-Spirits" or properties of nature described by the author; here, he describes them in their "enkindled" state of wrath or darkness.</note> generate themselves in this way:
I. First, the hardness generates a hard, raw, *rough, cold, and astringent quality*.
II. Second, the sweetness has grown *faint*, like a glowing coal when there is no more sap in the wood; it *gasps*, and there is *no refreshment* for it.
III. Third, the bitterness tears like a *hot plague* and is as *bitter as gall*.
IV. Fourth, the fire *burns* like a fierce, wrathful <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Sulphur"; in 17th-century alchemy and philosophy, sulfur was associated with the "burning" or "soul" quality of a substance.</note>.
V. Fifth, love is an *enmity* here.
VI. Sixth, the sound is a mere pounding, *rumbling, or cracking*, like the noise of a fire breaking out of a hollow place, as if it were great claps of thunder.
VII. Seventh, the surrounding region or *residence* of the body is a house of *mourning*.

120. Their food is an *abomination* and grows from the fierceness of all these qualities: lamentation and woe—and that forever, without end, for there is no "time" there. *Another King* sits on their throne, who holds judgment forever; they are merely his *footstool*.

121. O beauty, *pleasure*, and sensuality <note>original: "Voluptuousnesse"</note> of this world! O *riches* and proud stateliness! O might and *power*! Your unrighteous judgment and great pomp, with all your pleasure and sensuality, lie all together in a heap and have become a hellish fire!

122. Now eat and drink, now adorn and dress yourself with them, and rule over them, you fair *Goddess* <note>The author is likely addressing the soul that has turned toward worldly vanity rather than God.</note>.

# The Eleventh Chapter.

## VII.

### *Of the Seventh Qualifying or Fountain Spirit* <term>Qualifying spirit: A spirit that possesses specific qualities and actively contributes to the formation of the divine nature.</term>
### *in the Divine Power.*

->1.<-

**T**he Seventh Spirit of God in the Divine Power is the *Corpus* <note>Latin: "Body"</note> or Body, which is generated out of the other *six* spirits; it is the spirit in which *all* heavenly figures exist <note>original: "subsist"</note>, in which all things image and form themselves, and in which all beauty and joy rise up.

2. This is the very spirit of Nature—yes, *Nature itself*—in which comprehensibility <note>original: "apprehensibility or comprehensibility"</note> consists, and in which all creatures are formed in Heaven and on Earth. Yes, *Heaven itself* is formed within it; and *Naturality* <term>Naturality: The state of having a physical or substantial nature; the "material" aspect of the divine realm.</term> in the whole Deity consists in *this Spirit*.

3. If it were not for this Spirit, there would be neither angel nor man, and God would be an *unsearchable Being*, existing only in an *unsearchable* Power.

->*Question.*<-

4. Now the question is: How is this formed? Or in what manner is this so?

### Answer

If you are a <term>rational Mercurial spirit</term> <note>original: "Rational Mercurial spirit"; in Boehme’s alchemy-influenced theology, this refers to an active, searching, and transformative intellect</note> that *presses* through all the seven Spirits of God and beholds, proves, and examines them—discovering how they are—then through the explanation of this seventh Spirit, you will conceive and understand the *operation* and the *being* of the whole Deity, and grasp it in your own mind.

<margin>Gregory Richter, the Chief Pastor or Superintendent of the clergy at Görlitz.</margin>

5. "But if you *understand* nothing by this Spirit, then leave this book alone, and do not *judge* <note>original: "Richte"; a pun on the name of his critic, Richter, which means "judge"</note> the coldness or the warmth within it; for you are too tightly bound and imprisoned in *Saturn* <note>original: "Saturnus"; in this context, it refers to a spiritual state of darkness, rigidity, or worldly melancholy</note>, and are not a philosopher in this world."

6. Leave your *judging* <note>original: "Richten"</note> alone, or else you will receive your evil wages for it; therefore, I have faithfully warned you. Wait until you enter the next life, for then the heavenly gate will be opened to you, and then you will also understand this.

->Now observe the depth.<-

7. Here I must take hold of the entire divine body in the middle, at the heart, and explain the whole body and how nature exists. There you will see *the highest foundation*—how all the seven Spirits of God *continually* generate one another, and *how the Deity has neither beginning nor end.*

8. Therefore, behold and see the long-desired pleasure of your spirit, the eternal divine *joyfulness*, and the heavenly delight and bodily joy, which in all eternity has *no end.*

->**Now Observe.**<-

9. When the flash rises in the center, the divine birth stands in its full operation. In God, it is continually and eternally this way; but it is *not* so for us, poor fleshly children.

10. In this life, the triumphant divine birth lasts in us human beings only as long as the flash lasts; therefore, our *knowledge is only partial* <note>original: "but in part," a reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9</note>, whereas in God, the flash remains unchangeably and eternally present.

11. Behold, all seven Spirits of God are generated together at once; none of them is the first, and none of them is the last. However, we must keep our eye on the "kernel" <term>the core essence</term> and consider how the divine birth or "geniture" <term>the process of being born or generated</term> rises up; otherwise, a person cannot understand it.

12. Created beings cannot comprehend all seven Spirits within one another *at once*, but they can observe them. Yet, when one Spirit is touched or stirred, it touches or stirs all the others, and then the birth or "geniture" <note>original: "Geniture"</note> exists in its full power.

13. Therefore, it has a beginning in *humanity*, but no beginning in *God*. For this reason, I must also write in a "creaturely" manner <note>writing from the perspective of a finite, created being</note>, or else you could not understand it.

14. Behold, without the flash, all seven Spirits would be like a dark valley. But when the *flash* rises up between the astringent <term>the contracting or binding quality</term> and bitter qualities within the heat, it becomes shining in the "sweet water" <note>a mystical term for the divine essence or sap of life</note>. In the flames of the heat, it becomes bitter, triumphant, and living; and in the astringent, it becomes corporeal <term>physical or having a body</term>, dry, and *bright*.

<summary>Boehme explains the difference between God's eternal state of divine birth and humanity's fleeting, partial experience of it. He describes how the seven Spirits of God interact simultaneously, sparked into a living, physical brightness by the divine "flash."</summary>

### Chapter 11: In the Divine Power

15. Now these four Spirits move within the flash, for all four become living in it. The power of these four rises up in the flash as if *Life* itself were rising. This *power* that has risen in the flash is *Love*, which is *the fifth Spirit*.

16. This power moves so very pleasantly and lovely in the flash, as if a dead spirit were becoming alive and was suddenly, in a moment, placed into great clarity or *brightness*.

17. In this movement, one power touches or stirs another. First, the astringent <term>the contracting or "binding" quality in Boehme's physics</term> beats or strikes, and the heat creates a clear ringing sound from that stroke. The bitter power divides the ringing, and the water makes it mild and soft, thus mitigating it. This is *the sixth Spirit*.

18. Now the Tone in all *five* spirits rises up like a melodious, pleasant *music* and remains there; for the astringent quality dries it up <note>original: exsiccateth</note>.

19. So now, in that same sound that has gone forth—which now remains because it has been dried—is the power of all *six* qualifying or fountain spirits <note>the fundamental forces or "sources" of divinity</note>. It is, as it were, the *Seed* of the other six spirits, which they have gathered or incorporated together to make a Spirit. This spirit possesses the qualities of all the others, and that is the *Seventh Spirit of God* in the divine power.

## The Holy Gates.

### 32.
But the *Light*, which exists in the midst or center of all the Seven Spirits, is where the *Life* of all the seven Spirits resides; and by this Light, all seven become triumphant and joyful, and within it, heavenly *joyfulness* rises up.

33. This Light is *that* which all the seven spirits generate; it is the *Son* of all the seven spirits, and the seven spirits are its *Father*, for they generate the Light. In turn, the Light generates *Life* within them, and the *Light* is the Heart of the seven spirits. <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Seven Fountain Spirits" are the fundamental forces of God's nature that constantly interact to create all of existence.</note>

# 34. *And this Light is the true Son of God, whom we Christians worship and honor as the Second Person in the Holy Trinity.*

66. Do they not all grow out of the earth? Do they not stand next to one another? Does one *grudge* <note>original: "grutch"; meaning to envy or feel resentment</note> the beautiful form of the other?

# The Bridegroom Crowns His Bride.

79. Guess, friend, where does the crown lie? Toward the *North*; for in the center of the astringent <term>astringent: referring to the "cold" or contracting force in the author's theosophical system</term> quality, the light will be clear and bright.

81. What do those toward the *South* do? They have fallen asleep in the heat, but a stormy tempest will awaken them, and many among them will be terrified to death.

## Of this we will speak in its proper Place.

116. This, as mentioned above, is that fair, bright, and holy Heaven which exists within the total Deity <note>original: "Deitie"</note>. It has neither beginning nor end, and no creature can reach it with its senses.

117. Yet you shall know this: that in any given place, *one quality suddenly shows itself more powerfully* than the others. Suddenly the second prevails, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, and then suddenly the seventh. 

118. Thus, there is an *eternal wrestling, working*, and *friendly, amiable rising up of Love*. In this rising up, the Deity *continually shows itself to be more and more wonderful, more incomprehensible*, and more unsearchable.

119. So that the holy angels cannot rejoice enough, nor can they sufficiently converse, walk, and most lovingly play <note>original: "sport"</note> therein. 120. For the qualities rise up *eternally*, and so there is no beginning, middle, or end with them or among them.

12. Just as every *flower* in the meadows receives its color from its own quality and is named according to that quality, so it is with the holy angels. # Ch. XII. *Of the Nativity and Life of the Holy Angels:*

Wherever the love of God is awakened or stirred up, it stands there in the *full* birth or <term>geniture</term> <note>original: "geniture"; the process of generating or bringing into being</note> of the *whole* Deity, within the place or thing where it is awakened.

61. And in this, there is *no* difference: the angels are created one as well as another, *all* out of the Divine <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Jacob Boehme's term for the divine substance or "saltpeter" of the heavenly world</note> of the heavenly nature. The only difference between them is this: that when God constituted them, each quality in the "Great Motion" stood at its *highest* birth or rising up.

62. From this, it has come to pass that the angels have *various* and manifold qualities, and have different colors and beauties, and yet all come from God.

63. Yet *every* angel has *all* the qualities of God within him, but one of them is strongest in him; he is named according to that quality and glorified in it.

64. Now, as the qualities in God *always* generate, raise up, and heartily love one another, and each always receives its *life* from the other; and as the "flash" in the "sweet water" rises up in the heat—from which life and joy have their origin—so it is also in an angel. His *internal* birth or generation is no different than that which is distinct from him or outside of him in God.

65. And, just as the Son of God, distinct from the angels, is generated in the middle or central fountain-*spring*, in the heat, in the "sweet water," out of *all* the seven spirits of God, and shines back to re-enlighten all the seven spirits of God—*from which* they have their life and joy;

He is a king and prince of God upon the Mount of God, and has his office in the <term>Deep</term> <note>original: Deep; the vast, infinite spiritual space or dimension of the divine realm</note> in which he was created.

127. That circumference or space, region or province, in which he and his angels were created, is **his kingdom**. He is a **loving son** of God the Father in nature—a **creaturely son** in whom the Father delights.

128. You must **not compare** him with the Heart or Light of God <note>This refers to the Second Person of the Trinity, the eternal Word or Son, who is uncreated</note>, which exists in the whole Father and has neither beginning nor end, just like God the Father himself.

129. For this prince **is a creature** and has a beginning, but he is **in** God the Father and is bound and united with him **in his love**, as his dearly beloved son whom he has created out of himself.

And this is one King, rightly described with a true foundation in the knowledge of the Spirit.

## Of the second King LUCIFER, *so now called because of his Fall.*

131. King LUCIFER, shut your eyes here for a moment and stop your ears for a moment, so that you may neither hear nor see; or else you will be horribly ashamed that another sits upon your seat. Thus your shame shall be fully revealed before the end of the world—a shame which you have kept so closely concealed in secret and suppressed ever since the beginning of the world, wherever you could. I will now describe your kingly primacy <note>original: "Primacie"; supreme rank or the state of being first</note>, not for your sake, but for the *benefit of mankind.*

132. This high and mighty, glorious and beautiful king lost his true name in his fall; for he is now called LUCIFER, which means "one carried forth" or "expelled out of the light of God" <note>The author here provides a spiritual interpretation of the name; the Latin *Lucifer* traditionally translates to "Light-bringer"</note>.

127. His name was *not so in the beginning*, for he was a created prince or king of the Heart of God in the bright light—indeed, the brightest among the three kings of the angels.

<margin>* Lucifer's [Creation]</margin>
## Of * His Creation.

134. Just as *Michael* is created according to the nature, manner, and attributes of God the Father; so was *Lucifer* created according to the nature, condition, and beauty of God the *Son*. Lucifer was bound to and joined with him in love, like a dear son or heart, and his own heart also stood in the center of Light, as if he had been God himself; and his beauty or brightness surpassed all others.

135. For his origin, source, or primary mother <note>original: "circumference conception or chiefest mother"</note> was the *Son* of God, and there he stood as a king or prince of God.

136. His court, province, place, region, or territory where he lived with his whole army or company—and where he became a *created being*, and which was his kingdom—is the created Heaven and this world, in which we now live with our King JESUS CHRIST.

137. For our King sits in divine omnipotence where King Lucifer once sat, and on the kingly throne of the *expelled* <note>original: "expulsed"</note> Lucifer; thus, the kingdom of King Lucifer has now become HIS. O Prince Lucifer, how do you like that?

138. Now, just as God the Father is bound and united in great love with his Son, so was King Lucifer also bound with King *Michael* in great love, as one heart or one God; for the fountain or well-spring of the Son of God reached even into the heart of Lucifer.
